title: Wheels and a Gyro in a Filter: The Wheels Tell the Gyro Its Bias When They Say the Robot Is Going Straight, and the Gyro Tells the Wheels They Slipped

questions.question: Why are the wheels a good teacher of the gyro's bias when the robot is going straight?
options: They have no noise when going straight
Their turn is nothing then and so is their error, so the difference is the bias
They are sampled faster than the gyro
They are not: the bias can only be learnt while turning
questions.explanation: The wheels are wrong by a share of the turn they report. Going straight they report none, so whatever the gyro reads then is its bias.

questions.question: With the wheels alone the heading ended out by:
questions.explanation: The wheels' turn was 3 percent off, and a slip halved it for 2 s. Together that left 3.1 degrees.

questions.question: With the gyro alone the heading ended out by:
questions.explanation: A bias of 0.01 rad/s added up for 120 s is 1.2 rad, about 68 degrees. A small bias is a large heading error given time.

questions.question: With the filter the heading ended out by:
questions.explanation: It learnt the bias as 0.0089 rad/s while the robot went straight, and refused the slip. The position ended 0.3 m out, against 1.8 m and 14.1 m.

questions.question: What happens to a difference that is far from the estimate?
options: It is used, with a smaller weight
It is refused as a slip
It is kept and averaged with the next one
questions.explanation: A gyro's bias does not jump. A difference several standard deviations from the estimate is a wheel that slipped, so it is refused and counted.

questions.question: Why is the filter's variance for a measurement larger when the wheels are turning?
options: The wheels are wrong by a share of their turn rate, so a faster turn is a less certain measurement
The gyro is noisier in a turn
The filter runs slower in a turn
The bias changes with the turn rate
questions.explanation: At 0.3 rad/s with wheels 5 percent wrong the measurement is uncertain by 0.015 rad/s, three times the gyro's noise, so it counts for much less.
